name: Chapter 9: Hydrocarbons
description: Alkanes, conformations, alkenes, Markovnikov and peroxide effect, alkynes, benzene, aromaticity, electrophilic substitution, directive influence and carcinogenicity

cards.definition: Compounds of carbon and hydrogen only

cards.term: Source of petrol, diesel, kerosene vs coal gas?
cards.definition: Petrol, diesel, kerosene: fractional distillation of petroleum. Coal gas: destructive distillation of coal.

cards.term: Least polluting domestic fuel per NCERT?
cards.definition: LPG (kerosene causes some pollution)
Saturated (alkanes, cycloalkanes), unsaturated (alkenes, alkynes) and aromatic
Tetrahedral, C at centre; H–C–H = 109.5°

cards.term: C–C and C–H bond lengths in alkanes?
cards.definition: 154 pm and 112 pm
Inert to acids, bases and other reagents: Latin parum affinis = little affinity
In coal mines and marshy places

cards.term: Isomers of C₄H₁₀ and their b.p.?
cards.definition: n-Butane (273 K) and isobutane / 2-methylpropane (261 K)
n-Pentane 309 K, isopentane (2-methylbutane) 301 K, neopentane (2,2-dimethylpropane) 282.5 K

cards.text: Number of structural isomers: C₆H₁₄ = {{c1::5}}, C₇H₁₆ = {{c2::9}}, C₁₀H₂₂ = {{c3::75}}.

cards.definition: n-Hexane, 2-methylpentane, 3-methylpentane, 2,3-dimethylbutane, 2,2-dimethylbutane

Carbon bonded to 1, 2, 3, 4 other carbons
Methane’s C is counted as primary
4° is also called neo/quaternary
2,2,4,4-Tetramethylpentane; 3,3-dimethylpentane
Longest chain has 6 C: 3-methylhexane
Lower locant should go to the alphabetically first group: 3-ethyl-5-methylheptane
Lowest sum, alphabetical order, sec ignored, isopropyl as one word

cards.term: What is hydrogenation, and which catalysts?
cards.definition:
Adding H₂ to alkenes/alkynes over finely divided Pt, Pd or Ni.
Pt and Pd work at room T; Ni needs higher T and p

cards.term: Alkane from alkyl halide with Zn and dil. HCl?
cards.definition: Reduction: CH₃Cl + H₂ → CH₄ + HCl (not fluorides)
Alkyl halide + Na in dry ether → higher alkane (even number of C): 2CH₃Br + 2Na → C₂H₆ + 2NaBr

cards.term: Why isn’t Wurtz used for odd-carbon alkanes? (Ex 9.25)
cards.definition: Two different halides give a mixture (e.g. CH₃Br + C₂H₅Br → ethane + propane + butane), hard to separate
Sodium carboxylate + soda lime (NaOH + CaO), heat → alkane with one C less + Na₂CO₃

cards.term: Salt needed to make propane by decarboxylation? (Problem 9.6)
cards.definition: Sodium butanoate (CH₃CH₂CH₂COONa)

Electrolysis of Na/K carboxylate gives an alkane with even C at the anode.
2CH₃COONa → C₂H₆ (+ CO₂, H₂ at cathode)

cards.term: Why can’t methane be made by Kolbe’s method?
cards.definition: Two alkyl radicals couple, so the product has at least 2 carbons

cards.text: At 298 K: C₁–C₄ are {{c1::gases}}, C₅–C₁₇ are {{c2::liquids}}, C₁₈ onwards are {{c3::solids}}.

cards.term: Why do alkanes dissolve grease but not in water?
cards.definition: Non-polar: like dissolves like

cards.term: Effect of branching on boiling point?
cards.definition: More branching → more spherical → less surface contact → lower b.p. (neopentane lowest)
High temperature (573–773 K) or diffused sunlight/UV

cards.term: Products of stepwise chlorination of methane?
cards.definition: CH₃Cl → CH₂Cl₂ → CHCl₃ → CCl₄

cards.term: Reactivity of halogens and of H atoms in halogenation?
cards.definition: Halogens: F₂ > Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂. H atoms: 3° > 2° > 1°.

cards.term: Why is iodination of alkanes done with HIO₃ or HNO₃?
cards.definition: It is slow and reversible; oxidant removes HI

cards.text: Free radical halogenation: {{c1::initiation}} (Cl₂ → 2Cl•), {{c2::propagation}} (CH₄ + Cl• → CH₃• + HCl; CH₃• + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + Cl•), {{c3::termination}} (radicals combine).

cards.term: Why does ethane form during chlorination of methane? (Ex 9.1)
cards.definition: Termination step: CH₃• + CH₃• → C₂H₆

cards.term: Why is Cl–Cl broken first in initiation?
cards.definition: Cl–Cl is weaker than C–C and C–H
−890 kJ/mol and −2875.84 kJ/mol
\[C_nH_{2n+2} + \frac{3n+1}{2} O_2 \rightarrow nCO_2 + (n+1)H_2O\]

cards.term: Use of carbon black from incomplete combustion?
cards.definition: Ink, printer ink, black pigments, fillers
CH₄ + O₂, Cu/523 K/100 atm: Methanol; CH₄ + O₂, Mo₂O₃: Methanal (HCHO); C₂H₆ + O₂, (CH₃COO)₂Mn: Ethanoic acid; (CH₃)₃CH + KMnO₄: 2-Methylpropan-2-ol

cards.definition: Anhydrous AlCl₃ + HCl → 2-methylpentane and 3-methylpentane
n-Alkanes (C ≥ 6) at 773 K, 10–20 atm over oxides of V, Mo or Cr on alumina → benzene and homologues

cards.term: Alkane that gives toluene by aromatization?
cards.definition: n-Heptane
At 1273 K over Ni: CH₄ + H₂O → CO + 3H₂ (industrial H₂)
Heating higher alkanes to break into lower alkanes and alkenes free radical e.g. dodecane at 973 K (Pt/Pd/Ni) → heptane + pentene
Spatial arrangements interconvertible by rotation about a C–C single bond
Repulsion between electron clouds of adjacent bonds; barrier 1–20 kJ/mol
Eclipsed: H atoms as close as possible. Staggered: as far apart as possible. Skew: anything in between.
Sawhorse: (i) eclipsed (ii) staggered
Newman: front C is a point, rear C a circle (i) eclipsed (ii) staggered

cards.term: Angle between H’s on one carbon in Newman/sawhorse projections?
cards.definition: 120°

cards.term: Which conformation of ethane is more stable, and by how much?
cards.definition: Staggered; about 12.5 kJ/mol

cards.term: Why can’t ethane conformers be isolated?
cards.definition: The 12.5 kJ/mol barrier is crossed easily at room temperature: rotation is almost free

cards.term: Do bond angles and lengths change between conformations?
cards.definition: No

cards.term: General formula of alkenes and why "olefins"?
cards.definition: \( C_nH_{2n} \); ethene forms an oily liquid with chlorine (olefin = oil forming)

cards.text:
C=C: one {{c1::σ}} bond (~397 kJ/mol, sp²–sp²) + one {{c2::π}} bond (~284 kJ/mol, sideways p–p)
total {{c3::681}} kJ/mol
length {{c4::134 pm}}.

cards.term: Why are alkenes attacked by electrophiles?
cards.definition: The π electrons are loosely held and exposed
σ framework of sp² orbitals π bond above and below the plane H–C–H ≈ 116.6°

cards.term: Bond angles and lengths in ethene (Fig 9.5)?
cards.definition: C=C 134 pm, C–H 110 pm, H–C–C 121.7°
But-1-ene, buta-1,3-diene, 2-methylprop-1-ene
But-1-ene, but-2-ene, 2-methylprop-1-ene
Pent-1-ene, pent-2-ene, 2-methylbut-2-ene, 3-methylbut-1-ene, 2-methylbut-1-ene

cards.term: Why does C=C show geometrical isomerism?
cards.definition: Restricted rotation about the double bond (like two cardboards nailed together)
Each doubly bonded carbon must carry two different groups (XYC=CXY, XYC=CXZ, XYC=CZW)
cis: identical groups on the same side. trans: opposite sides.

cards.term: Dipole moments of cis- and trans-but-2-ene?
cards.definition: cis 0.33 D; trans ≈ 0 (C–CH₃ dipoles cancel)

cards.term: Which has higher m.p. and which higher b.p.: cis or trans?
cards.definition: m.p.: trans (packs better). b.p.: cis (more polar).

cards.term: Which show cis–trans: (CH₃)₂C=CHC₂H₅, CH₂=CBr₂, C₆H₅CH=CHCH₃, CH₃CH=CClCH₃? (Problem 9.11)
cards.definition: Only C₆H₅CH=CHCH₃ and CH₃CH=CClCH₃

cards.term: What is Lindlar’s catalyst and its product?
cards.definition: Pd/C poisoned with S compounds or quinoline; alkyne → cis-alkene

cards.term: Alkyne + Na in liquid NH₃ gives?
cards.definition: trans-Alkene

cards.term: Does propene from propyne show geometrical isomerism?
cards.definition: No: one carbon has two H atoms
Alkyl halide + alcoholic KOH, heat → alkene; a β-elimination
Halogen: I > Br > Cl. Alkyl: 3° > 2° > 1°.

cards.term: What is a vicinal dihalide, and dehalogenation?
cards.definition: Halogens on adjacent carbons; with Zn → alkene + ZnX₂
Heat with conc. H₂SO₄ → alkene + H₂O (β-elimination)
First 3 gases, next 14 liquids, rest solids; ethene has a faint sweet smell
Reddish orange Br₂ in CCl₄ is decolourised

cards.term: Does iodine add to alkenes normally?
cards.definition: No

cards.term: Reactivity order of HX towards alkenes?
cards.definition: HI > HBr > HCl
The negative part of the adding molecule goes to the carbon with fewer H atoms

cards.term: Mechanism behind Markovnikov addition of HBr to propene?
cards.definition: H⁺ adds first to give the more stable 2° carbocation; Br⁻ then attacks → 2-bromopropane
"The rich get richer": H goes to the carbon that already has more H
With benzoyl peroxide, HBr adds anti-Markovnikov to propene → 1-bromopropane (free radical)
Morris S. Kharasch (with F.R. Mayo, 1933, Chicago)

cards.term: Why no peroxide effect with HCl and HI?
cards.definition: H–Cl (430.5 kJ/mol) is too strong to break; I• radicals combine to I₂ instead of adding
Br• adds to C-1 giving the more stable 2° free radical

cards.term: Hex-1-ene + HBr without and with peroxide? (Problem 9.12)
cards.definition: Without: 2-bromohexane. With: 1-bromohexane.
Markovnikov addition → alkyl hydrogen sulphate
With a few drops of conc. H₂SO₄ → alcohol (Markovnikov)

cards.term: What is Baeyer’s reagent and its product?
cards.definition: Cold dilute aqueous KMnO₄ → vicinal glycols; decolourisation = test for unsaturation
2 CH₃COOH (ethanoic acid)
O₃ adds to give an ozonide, cleaved by Zn–H₂O into carbonyls; locates the double bond

cards.term: Alkene giving ethanal and pentan-3-one on ozonolysis? (Ex 9.5)
cards.definition: 3-Ethylpent-2-ene: CH₃CH=C(C₂H₅)₂

cards.term: Alkene with 3 C–C σ, 8 C–H σ, 1 π that gives 2 mol of a 44 u aldehyde? (Ex 9.6)
cards.definition: But-2-ene (ozonolysis → 2 CH₃CHO)
Ethanal + propanal

cards.term: Monomers and uses of polythene and polypropene?
cards.definition: Ethene → polythene (bags, sheets, toys, pipes). Propene → polypropene (milk crates, buckets).
Oxyacetylene flame for arc welding

cards.term: Common names of propyne, but-1-yne, but-2-yne?
cards.definition: Methylacetylene, ethylacetylene, dimethylacetylene
Pent-1-yne, pent-2-yne, 3-methylbut-1-yne

Hex-1-yne
Hex-2-yne
Hex-3-yne
3-Methylpent-1-yne
4-Methylpent-1-yne
4-Methylpent-2-yne
3,3-Dimethylbut-1-yne

C≡C: one {{c1::σ}} (sp–sp) and two {{c2::π}} bonds
H–C–C = {{c3::180°}}
bond enthalpy {{c4::823}} kJ/mol
length {{c5::120 pm}}.

cards.term: Shape of the electron cloud in ethyne?
cards.definition: Cylindrically symmetrical about the axis: linear molecule
CaCO₃ → CaO CaO + 3C → CaC₂ + CO CaC₂ + 2H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ + C₂H₂
Alcoholic KOH (→ vinyl halide), then sodamide (NaNH₂)
First 3 gases, next 8 liquids, rest solids

cards.term: Why are terminal alkyne H atoms acidic?
cards.definition: sp carbon (50% s) is most electronegative, so C–H electrons are pulled in and H⁺ leaves easily

cards.term: Acidity order: ethyne, ethene, ethane? And ethyne, propyne, but-2-yne?
cards.definition: HC≡CH > CH₂=CH₂ > CH₃CH₃; HC≡CH > CH₃C≡CH ≫ CH₃C≡CCH₃
Monosodium ethynide, then disodium ethynide, + H₂
Only but-1-yne (terminal H) reacts with Na/NaNH₂
Ethyne > benzene > n-hexane (sp > sp² > sp³)

cards.term: HBr adds to ethyne twice: final product?
cards.definition: 1,1-Dibromoethane (a gem-dihalide)

cards.term: Hydration of alkynes: conditions and product?
cards.definition: HgSO₄ + dil. H₂SO₄ at 333 K → carbonyl compound (ethyne → ethanal)

cards.term: What is polyacetylene and its use?
cards.definition: Linear polymer of ethyne; conducts electricity (films as battery electrodes)
Red hot iron tube, 873 K: 3C₂H₂ → benzene
CH₃COONa + soda lime → CH₄ → CH₃Cl → C₂H₆ (Wurtz) → C₂H₄Br₂ … → C₂H₂ → red hot Fe tube → benzene
Greek "aroma" (pleasant smell). Benzenoid: contain a benzene ring. Non-benzenoid: aromatic without one.
Michael Faraday, 1825

cards.term: Evidence for three double bonds in benzene?
cards.definition: Forms a triozonide

Alternate single/double bonds in a ring.
Problem: it predicts two 1,2-dibromobenzenes but only one exists → oscillating bonds

cards.term: What does Kekulé’s structure fail to explain?
cards.definition: Benzene’s unusual stability and preference for substitution over addition

cards.term: C–C bond length in benzene vs C–C and C=C?
cards.definition: 139 pm (all equal), between 154 pm and 133–134 pm
Six sp² carbons; unhybridised p orbitals overlap all around → two "doughnut" π clouds above and below the ring

cards.text: Aromaticity (Hückel): {{c1::planar}} ring, {{c2::complete delocalisation}} of π electrons, and {{c3::(4n + 2)}} π electrons.

cards.definition: n = 1 (6π): benzene, cyclopentadienyl anion, cycloheptatrienyl cation. n = 2 (10π): naphthalene.
Cyclic polymerisation of ethyne decarboxylation of sodium benzoate (soda lime) reduction of phenol by hot zinc dust
Coal tar
With a sooty flame
Moth repellent; toilets
Benzene + R–X or RCOCl/(RCO)₂O with anhydrous AlCl₃ → alkylbenzene / acylbenzene
The 1° carbocation rearranges to the more stable 2° carbocation
Hexachlorobenzene (C₆Cl₆)

cards.text: SE mechanism: generation of {{c1::electrophile}} → formation of {{c2::σ-complex (arenium ion)}} → loss of {{c3::proton}} to restore aromaticity.

cards.term: How is the nitronium ion formed?
cards.definition: H₂SO₄ protonates HNO₃ (HNO₃ acts as a base); loses water → NO₂⁺

cards.term: Why is the arenium ion not aromatic?
cards.definition: One carbon becomes sp³, breaking delocalisation

cards.term: Why does benzene prefer electrophilic substitution? (Ex 9.19)
cards.definition:
The electron-rich π cloud attracts electrophiles.
Substitution keeps the ring aromatic (addition would lose it)
H₂/Ni, high T and p → cyclohexane. Cl₂ in UV → benzene hexachloride C₆H₆Cl₆.

cards.term: Correction: NCERT says benzene hexachloride "is also called gammaxane". Accurate?
cards.definition: BHC is a mixture of isomers; only the γ-isomer (lindane) is gammaxane, the insecticide

cards.term: General combustion equation of a hydrocarbon?
cards.definition: \[C_xH_y + (x + \frac{y}{4})O_2 \rightarrow xCO_2 + \frac{y}{2}H_2O\]
The group already present (not the incoming one) decides whether the new group goes o/p or m

cards.term: Why is –OH ortho/para directing and activating?
cards.definition: Its +R effect raises electron density at o and p; outweighs its −I effect
–NH₂, –NHR, –NHCOCH₃, –OCH₃, –CH₃, –C₂H₅, –OH

cards.term: Why are halogens deactivating yet o/p directing?
cards.definition: Strong −I lowers overall density (deactivating); +R keeps o/p richer than m
–NO₂, –CN, –CHO, –COR, –COOH, –COOR, –SO₃H
Its −I and −R pull electrons from o and p; meta is left comparatively richer

cards.term: Ease of nitration: benzene, m-dinitrobenzene, toluene? (Ex 9.23)
cards.definition: Toluene > benzene > m-dinitrobenzene
p-Nitrobromobenzene: brominate first, then nitrate. m-Nitrochlorobenzene: nitrate first, then chlorinate.
"Lone pair on the first atom → o/p; a multiple bond to an electronegative atom → meta"
Benzene and polynuclear hydrocarbons with more than two fused benzene rings

cards.term: How are carcinogenic PAHs formed and how do they harm?
cards.definition: Incomplete combustion of tobacco, coal, petroleum; they damage DNA
Alkanes: Free radical substitution; Alkenes: Electrophilic addition; Alkynes: Electrophilic addition; terminal H acidic; Arenes: Electrophilic substitution
